title: Bounded worker pool for inventory reservations
name: Inventory reservation pool

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how the worker pool tracks and frees its concurrency slots? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: In BoundedPool.run, `this.active--` only executes on the success path. When a task rejects (e.g. an inventory reserve times out), the catch branch rejects the caller but never decrements `active`. Each failure permanently leaks a slot; after `concurrency` failures `active` stays at the limit, drain() never starts anything, queued work piles up until maxQueued, and every new order gets PoolSaturatedError. The decrement belongs in a finally block (or before both branches).

choiceQuestions.prompt: With concurrency 8 and an order of 20 lines submitted while the pool is idle, what happens immediately inside submit/drain?
choices: All 20 inventory calls start at once; the limit only applies across orders
8 calls start and 12 jobs wait in the queue until running ones finish
8 calls start and the remaining 12 submits are rejected with PoolSaturatedError
Calls run one at a time because drain() awaits each task
choiceQuestions.explanation: Each submit pushes onto the queue and calls drain(), which starts jobs only while active < concurrency, so 8 run and 12 wait. The limit is per pool instance, shared by all orders, not per order. Saturation only happens when the queue length reaches maxQueued (500). drain() does not await run(); it fires it and keeps looping.

choiceQuestions.prompt: When some lines of an order succeed and at least one fails, what does reserveOrder return or do?
choices: Returns the successful reservation IDs and the failed SKUs so the caller can retry only the failures
Throws immediately without touching the successful reservations
Releases the successful reservations through the pool and returns an empty reservations list with the failed SKUs
Retries the failed SKUs once before giving up
choiceQuestions.explanation: The branch `failedSkus.length > 0 && reservations.length > 0` submits release calls for each reservation through the pool and returns `reservations: []` with the failed SKUs, making the order all-or-nothing. It does not return partial reservations, does not throw in this branch, and contains no retry.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Why does the service use Promise.allSettled rather than Promise.all over the submitted reservations?
choices: allSettled runs the promises with lower concurrency than Promise.all
allSettled waits for every line's outcome so all successful reservations are known and can be released on partial failure
Promise.all would cancel in-flight inventory requests when one fails, wasting work
choiceQuestions.explanation: Promise.all would reject on the first failure while other reserves are still in flight, so the service would not learn which reservations succeeded and could not release them. allSettled waits for all outcomes. It does not affect concurrency (the pool does), does not retry, and Promise.all cannot cancel underlying requests.
